sources_considered.why: Primary study of instruction-following mechanisms, including causal ablations.
Methods and limitations clarify what the ablations establish.
Primary causal analysis of reasoning processes provides evidence both of spurious correlations and of improvement through training.
Behavioral failure rates do not identify the cause of those failures.

evidence_items.publisher: Elisabetta Rocchetti and Alfio Ferrara, arXiv
evidence_items.locator: Abstract, third finding; revised version dated 2026-09-10
evidence_items.explanation: The study finds task-dependent organization of instruction-following skills in three models. Its ablations concern representations and diagnostic probes; they do not establish that failure to represent causation causes the instruction violations Marcus describes.

The authors report causal weaknesses in some reasoning processes and stronger causal patterns after reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards. This complicates the blanket correlation-versus-causation description, but does not directly test the claimed explanation for instruction failures.

unresolved_gaps: No retrieved study directly isolates the proposed cause of the instruction failures described in the post.
The available studies use limited model samples and different meanings of causal structure.
Evidence of statistical prediction, instruction failure, and causal-reasoning weakness does not by itself establish a causal chain between them.
